# Active AI Reading

> A course where we read AI papers actively: we summarize, critique, redraw, reimplement and share them, written by the students.

Students of a graduate course read one AI research paper per week and publish what they make of it: rewritten abstracts, critiques, redrawn figures, reimplementations, literature maps, follow-up ideas and social media posts. Each paper page collects everything written about that paper.

## Papers

- [Matryoshka Language Model Suites](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/papers/matryoshka-lm-suites/): Nathan Godey, Yoav Artzi, 2026 (arXiv 2608.09703)
- [Why Pretraining Fails to Share Cross-Lingual Knowledge](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/papers/cross-lingual-knowledge-pretraining/): Bilingual LLMs learn the same fact twice, once per language, and the cause is largely tokenization: two copies of English with disjoint token IDs already fail to share knowledge. Mapping Arabic words into English tokens (word-wise translation) makes knowledge transfer 14× better. (arXiv 2609.19291)
- [Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/papers/recurrent-depth-latent-reasoning/): Jonas Geiping, Sean McLeish, Neel Jain, John Kirchenbauer, Siddharth Singh, Brian R. Bartoldson, Bhavya Kailkhura, Abhinav Bhatele, Tom Goldstein, 2025 (arXiv 2502.05171)

## Posts

- [Rewriting the Matryoshka Abstract: Making Technical Concepts More Intuitive](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/matryoshka-abstract-chenshani-droid/): Explaining nested language models and speculative decoding for readers unfamiliar with these concepts. (Writing, on "Matryoshka Language Model Suites", 2026-10-25)
- [Visualizing Core ideas](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/main-visual-matryoshka-lm-suites/): One figure showing how three separate models become one nested model, how the blocks connect, and how the smaller models learn from the largest. (Visualization, on "Matryoshka Language Model Suites", 2026-10-25)
- [Video explainer for Matryoshka LM Suites](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/extras-matryoshka-lm-suites/): Video explainer for Matryoshka LM Suites. (Communicate to the world, on "Matryoshka Language Model Suites", 2026-10-25)
- [Rewriting the abstract of Matryoshka Language Model Suites](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/abstract-matryoshka-lm-suites/): Making the comparisons clearer, with a trade-off in technical detail. (Writing, on "Matryoshka Language Model Suites", 2026-10-25)
- [What Makes a Chain of Thought Easy to Learn?](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/what-makes-a-chain-of-thought-easy-to-learn/): How teacher-generated reasoning can help smaller models learn, and why the structure of a reasoning trace might matter. (Learning to learn, on "Matryoshka Language Model Suites", 2026-10-24)
- [The points that matter about Matryoshka suites.](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/week1-The-points-that-matter/): A quick recap on what you need to remember from this paper instead of re-reading everything. (Writing, on "Matryoshka Language Model Suites", 2026-10-24)
- [Rewriting the abstract](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/rewriting-the-abstract-matryoshka-lm-suites/): Why should we care about language model suites ? (Writing, on "Matryoshka Language Model Suites", 2026-10-24)
- [Reimplementing a speculative decoding throughput test, shown in Figure 5a](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/reimplement-cross-lingual-knowledge-pretraining/): I implemented a speculative decoding throughput performance test, running the 500M model as a draft model and the full 3B model as the verifier, examining a speedup against a baseline (Coding, on "Matryoshka Language Model Suites", 2026-10-24)
- [A better Figure 2](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/redo-graph-figure-2/): Figure 2 uses two ternary plots to select a model architecture, but the key tradeoff between memory and computation is hidden across separate panels (Visualization, on "Matryoshka Language Model Suites", 2026-10-24)
- [Three models in one: a toy Matryoshka suite vs. three separate models](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/matryoshka-toy/): One nested transformer with three exits, trained once, against three separate models of matched size. The shape of the paper's result holds at toy scale. (Coding, on "Matryoshka Language Model Suites", 2026-10-24)
- [Literature review of Matryoshka Language Model Suites](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/literature-matryoshka-lm-suites/): Ideas behind Matryoshka LM Suites and what it adds (Research skills, on "Matryoshka Language Model Suites", 2026-10-24)
- [A new way of speculative decoding and on policy distillation](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/hidden-gems-matryoshka-lm-suites/): 2 papers that expand on ideas used in the matryoshka suits paper. (Paper scouting, on "Matryoshka Language Model Suites", 2026-10-24)
- [Follow-ups of Matryoshka Language Model Suites](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/follow-ups-matryoshka-lm-suites/): The nested suite was built for efficiency, but its shared backbone makes it a ready-made interpretability testbed. (Research skills, on "Matryoshka Language Model Suites", 2026-10-24)
- [Is nesting the cheapest way to build a model suite?](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/follow-ups-matryoshka-lm-suites-eylonkrause/): Five follow-ups that test the paper's efficiency claims, all starting from checkpoints the authors have already released. (Research skills, on "Matryoshka Language Model Suites", 2026-10-24)
- [Figure 2 in layers and dimentions annotations in the Matryoshka article](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/figure-2-in-layers/): changing the paper's triangles' ticks with layer counts and possible embedding dimensions for easier undderstanding (Visualization, on "Matryoshka Language Model Suites", 2026-10-24)
- [Copyediting Section 1 (Introduction) of Matryoshka Language Model Suites](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/copyedit-introduction-matryoshka-lm-suites/): Removing repetition. (Writing, on "Matryoshka Language Model Suites", 2026-10-24)

- [How autoregressive and diffusion LMs imitate each other, and why it is inefficient](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/autoregressive-vs-diffusion/): A claim from week 1, made easier to follow with pictures: each model type can do what the other does, and what it costs to do so. - [Reimplementing CLeq: what does 12.6% actually mean?](https://active-ai-reading.github.io/posts/2026/reimplementing-cleq/): I simulated the paper's measurement with a known amount of transfer.
